newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ZALAKERAMIA PLANS TO RAISE $40 MLN.
newsitem.headline: ZALAKERAMIA PLANS TO RAISE $40 MLN.

text.p: Hungary's leading tile maker Zalakeramia Rt said on Monday it was planning to raise $40 million from a private placement whose revenue is to be spent on investments in its recent acquisitions.
"Zalakeramia is preparing for a $40 million capital increase," Finance Director Agnes Albrecht told the company's annual shareholders meeting.

Zalakeramia's shareholders approved in March a private capital increase via the issue of new shares between 900,000 and 1,200,000 units, with Credit Suisse First Boston and Raiffeisen Zentral Bank acting as lead managers.
Roadshows are going between April 18 and May 3.
In 1997 Zalakeramia has bought a 79.3 percent stake in Croatia's Inker and a 59 percent stake in Hungary's Pietra.
Zalakeramia's chairman John T. Rourke said the company was planning to invest some $26 million in Inker and $11.5 million in Pietra. Investments include capacity increase and debt relief in both.
Zalakeramia was also planning to boost its stake further in Pietra. "We'll continue to buy until we have a substantial majority," Rourke said.
Pietra is Hungary's third largest tile maker with a six percent market share and has a capacity of an annual one million square metres of wall cover and 600,000 square metres of floor cover.
Zalakeramia's total capacity is around 5.5 million square metres without Pietra.
Inker produces sanitery products, porcelainware for hotels and decoration tiles.
Zalakeramia Rt will pay an 11 percent dividend on its 1996 earnings, up from 10 percent last year, following shareholders' approval. Dividend payments will start on May 23.

In 1996 Zalakeramia generated HAS after-tax profit of 875.9 million forints on net sales of 3.829 billion forints, up from an after-tax profit of 357.6 million on net sales of 3.070 billion forints in 1995.
